predictions: P-A (BB union rule): the new fits will pass the union rule (LRT_BANDBB_BAND>=9.2 & kT>1.05 OR LRT_CPLBB_CPL>=9.2 & kT>1.05) in >=3 resolved blocks, and those blocks will be CONTIGUOUS and EARLY - the first ~4 s after trigger - with the union-block kT population in 20-45 keV and a MONOTONIC DECLINE of kT with time. Archival: union blocks {2,3,4} = 3 resolved, kT 40.97 / 30.31 / 22.60 keV, strictly decreasing; integrated block NOT in the union (LRT_BANDBB_BAND=0.61). This is the HIGH-kT class, not the L28 edge-constrained low-kT class - the BB here sits near ~3*kT ~ 100 keV, well above the NaI floor, so it is NOT a fit-edge artifact. FALSIFIED IF: the union count in resolved blocks drops to <=1, or the union-block kT population moves below 15 keV or above 60 keV, or kT stops declining monotonically across the union blocks.

P-A2 (the union rule will now ALSO fire on the integrated block, and that is the sharpest single test in this freeze): the archival integrated block is a clean union-rule FAILURE (LRT_BANDBB_BAND=0.61, kT=1.344 keV; LRT_CPLBB_CPL=0.00) - i.e. our previous production run found NO thermal component in the time-integrated spectrum. FOUR independent published groups disagree: Axelsson+2012 (time-integrated Band C=1078/618 -> Band+BB 901/616, '>5 sigma'), Aldowma+2026 (GBM+LAT+LLE over 0.003-21.825 s, ISSM+BB with kT=35+/-2.7 keV, stat improvement 42), Chang+2026 (0-20 s, Band+BB wins their 6-model menu), Li An+2024 (-2.048-3.072 s, Band+BB, kT=34.419 keV). PREDICT: with the L8/L9/L18-L20 hardening, the integrated block yields LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 with kT in 25-45 keV. FALSIFIED IF: the integrated LRT_BANDBB_BAND stays < 9.2 - in which case the defect is OURS (an integration-over-a-sweeping-Ep pathology or an optimizer local minimum), not a literature error, and it must be reported as such.

P-A3 (blk1 negative-LRT defect must not survive): the archival blk1 [0.081,0.470] has LRT_BANDBB_BAND = -0.00, which is mathematically impossible for a nested pair (lesson L-C, raised on this very burst). Axelsson finds kT=62 (+10/-8.8) keV with dC=25 over an overlapping interval. PREDICT: blk1 returns a POSITIVE LRT_BANDBB_BAND. FALSIFIED IF: any nested LRT in this burst is again <= 0 - which would mean the L-C hardening never landed.

P-B (literature frame, EARLY blocks - the Ep sweep): the first resolved block will return an EXTREME Ep. Three independent frames bracket it: Axelsson+2012 13-bin first bin [-0.32,0.0] Ep = 15 +/- 2 MeV (Band+BB decomposition); Zhang B.+2012 Band-only [-0.512,0.064] Ep = 19.56 +/- 4.22 MeV; Yu+2016 catalog bin 1 [-1.024,0.711] COMP Ep = 7409 +/- 597 keV. The three are NOT in conflict - they are three different decompositions over three different intervals, and Yu+2016 states its own value is '2 sigma consistent' with Axelsson's LOWER-resolution first bin (5410 +410/-420 keV). PREDICT: our first block, being Band-family and Band-ONLY-like, lands in the 7-20 MeV decade, i.e. ABOVE the Band+BB decompositions and consistent with Zhang's Band-only 19.56 MeV. Archival blk0 was RAILED at Ep=5000.00 keV (the old 5 MeV cap, lesson L9) so the archival value is a bound, not a measurement. FALSIFIED IF: the first block returns Ep < 3 MeV with a well-constrained (non-railed, MINOS-OK) error, or rails again at any bound.

P-B2 (evolution class - a falsifiable NON-monotonic prediction): Ep is hard-to-soft through the bright phase and then RE-HARDENS. Two independent published claims: Wang+2024 - 'One burst (GRB 110721A) demonstrated a hard-to-soft evolution followed by soft-to-hard pattern', the ONLY such burst in their 28-burst single-pulse set; Duan+2020 - evolution column 'h.t.s./s.t.h. to h.t.s.'. Everyone else (GCN 12191 Konus, Basak & Rao 2014, Yu+2016, Li&Zhang 2021) calls it plain hard-to-soft, which is what a coarse binning would see. Archival Band Ep does turn back up: 5000(railed) -> 4943 -> 1481 -> 262 -> 246 -> 458 -> 470 -> 316 -> 403 -> 373 keV, i.e. a MINIMUM near 3-3.7 s followed by a factor ~1.9 re-hardening. PREDICT: block-resolved Ep reaches a minimum in the block covering ~3.0-3.7 s and then rises by >30% in the following 1-2 blocks. FALSIFIED IF: Ep decays monotonically to the end of the window, or the post-minimum rise is < 1 sigma.

P-B3 (two-break support): LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 will persist in the INTEGRATED spectrum (archival 40.74) and in the brightest early blocks (archival blk2 78.38, blk3 22.16, blk4 14.40). CRUCIAL CAVEAT declared in advance: over exactly these blocks the archival run ALSO has a significant BB (kT 41/30/23 keV), and a blackbody at kT~20-40 keV and a second SBPL break near ~3kT occupy the same decade - lesson L-G says the correct report there is DEGENERATE(SBPL+BB == 2SBPL), and only dAIC_simp ('is extra structure needed') may be quoted. So a DSBPL win in blocks 2-4 is NOT independent evidence of two breaks. The INFORMATIVE test is whether LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 survives in a block where the BB is ABSENT. Archival: no such block (blk1 6.42 and blk5 7.36 both fall short). PREDICT: the two-break signal in this burst remains BB-confounded and this burst contributes a DEGENERATE, not a clean two-break, entry to the census. FALSIFIED IF: any block with LRT_BANDBB_BAND < 2 returns LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2.

P-B4 (a NEW measurement no published analysis has made): no published analysis of this burst has ever fitted a 2SBPL / low-energy-break model (Axelsson: Band, Band+BB, Band+mBB; Zhang+2012: Band; Iyyani: BB+Band; Basak & Rao: Band, BBPL, mBBPL, 2BBPL; Aldowma+2026: ISSM(+BB)). 2SBPL is the synchrotron parameterisation. PREDICT: in the DSBPL-winning blocks the low-energy index pair will NOT land on the fast-cooling synchrotron values (-2/3 above, -3/2 below the cooling break) - because alpha is measured at -0.70 to -0.92 in exactly those blocks, HARDER than -2/3, which is the constraint Axelsson and Iyyani both use against optically-thin synchrotron. FALSIFIED IF: the DSBPL index pair lands within 1 sigma of (-2/3, -3/2) with a physically sensible break ratio.

P-C (Step 5 binning, external validation): our Bayesian-Blocks edges will again include ~0.470 s and ~6.252 s. Li & Zhang 2021 place their two HLE decay episodes as starting at 0.470 s and 6.252 s - identical to the archival blk2 and blk7 start times to 3 decimals, from independent code on the same TTE. PREDICT: both edges reproduce within 0.05 s. FALSIFIED IF: either edge moves by > 0.2 s. CAVEAT declared in advance: it is NOT yet verified that Li & Zhang's quantity is a block edge rather than a fitted decay start - if it is the latter, the agreement is evidence about the burst, not about our binning, and this prediction must be re-labelled rather than scored.

P-C2 (Step 7, temporal): T90 measured on a window >= 2x the expected duration will come out at 22-26 s, NOT the 15.17 s of the walkthrough run. Published: GBM 24.45 s (50-300 keV, GCN 12187), Konus ~25 s, Axelsson ~24.5 s, and the Li/Wang/Shao sample papers all carry T90 = 21.82 +/- 0.57 s (the GBM catalog value, 50-300 keV). Our 15.17 s is a WINDOW ARTEFACT - the block window is only 18.98 s long (lesson L-H). Energy-dependent MVT: Golkhou+2015 uses this burst as its worked example and gives Delta_t_min = 0.56/0.28/0.24/0.22 s for GBM channels 1-4 (softest->hardest); PREDICT our single-band MVT-Haar lands in 0.2-0.6 s and, if run per band, decreases with energy. Lag: Lu+2018 gives 0.40 +/- 0.11 s; our walkthrough lag_std was +0.685 s - a REAL frame difference (different band pairs, different definitions), to be aligned before it is called a discrepancy. FALSIFIED IF: T90 on the widened window still returns < 18 s.

P-D (identity, NOT a fit target): NO usable redshift. Two branches (z=0.382 CaII H&K or z=3.512 Ly-alpha, GCN 12193, no confirming lines at either) AND the IPN says the counterpart carrying those lines 'lies just outside the IPN error box, making it unlikely that it is related to the GRB' (GCN 12195). The literature splits: Duan+2020 / Yonetoku+2012 / Chang+2026 / Li An+2024 adopt 0.382; Aldowma+2026 adopts 3.512 (mis-citing Greiner GCN 12192, which has no spectroscopy); only Iyyani+2013 discloses the ambiguity (and adopts z=2 as an admitted placeholder). PREDICT: this burst is EXCLUDED from every rest-frame correlation in our paper and from the Gao&Zhang / registry-#43 Tier-B analysis. 9 GCN circulars; IPN position (332.456, -38.628) is the sample position; LAT-detected and NOT retracted; LLE + LAT data both on disk and both belong in the fit (L17). Step-1 D1: LLE DRM Delta_theta = 0.34 deg over the stamped window - VALID, Fermi did not slew.

P-E (sample definition, declared before the fit): this burst's SINGLE-PULSE membership is contested in print. Basak & Rao 2014: 'for GRB 110721A, we found that fitting two pulses is significantly better than a single pulse fitting (an improvement of Delta chi2 = 205.1 ... to the expense of 4 degrees of freedom)'; Preece+2016 Fig. 3: the NaI-9 256 ms light curve 'shows some deviation from a simple pulse profile at the peak'. PREDICT: our pulse-fitting step will also prefer 2 components over 1 at high significance. This is a CAVEAT to disclose, not a reason to drop the burst. FALSIFIED IF: a single Norris/FRED pulse is preferred over a two-pulse model.
